title: Scheduled Authorization Sweep and SCIM Reconciliation Orchestrator
creator: Ava Chen
description: Goal: Build an orchestrator that runs scheduled authorization sweeps across tenants, reconciles SCIM provisioning state with our internal RBAC graph, and emits signed, region-aware audit bundles suitable for downstream GRC ingestion. Scope: 1) periodic RBAC snapshots and change-deltas per tenant (owner-assigned); 2) SCIM reconciliation job that detects provisioning drift and raises automated remediation requests (or creates tickets for manual review); 3) SAML session correlation so access revocations and recent logins are reflected in review bundles; 4) export choreography to push encrypted audit bundles (with retention metadata) to customer-controlled S3 or internal vaults for on-demand compliance reporting. Success criteria: - Automated sweeps run on schedule with per-tenant cadence (daily/weekly/monthly) - Reconciliation accuracy > 98% for identity mappings in pilot tenants - Generated bundles contain RBAC snapshot, SCIM delta, and correlated SAML session summaries and are cryptographically signed - Exports include retention and residency metadata and respect per-tenant retention polices until proof-of-deletion is verifiable - Integration end-to-end for 3 enterprise pilots with review workflow in Console and downloadable ZIP bundles for auditors Design notes: - Orchestrator is a new service (stateless scheduler + worker pool) that leverages existing eventstream for incremental delta ingestion. - RBAC snapshot is derived from canonical auth store (Authorization Service) with tenant-scoped filters. - SCIM reconciliation uses a configurable scoping layer to avoid noisy churn for large orgs; supports dry-run mode. - Bundles are JSONL + manifest, signed with KMS per-region/keyspace; retention metadata added to manifest and S3 object tags. - Console additions: review queue (owner-assigned), one-click create access certification tasks, and manual override hooks. Rollout plan: alpha on 3 tenants (internal + 2 customers) -> iterate on reconciliation thresholds -> expand to all enterprise tenants. Rollback: disable scheduler and rely on on-demand snapshot export until issues resolved. Notes on residency & retention: retention windows are configurable per-tenant and per-region; orchestrator must resolve nearest region for export and attach residency claim to manifest. Security: service will use customer-scoped KMS keys where available; otherwise platform-managed keys with explicit consent.
comments: 2025-01-20: Spike complete. PoC generated RBAC snapshot + SCIM diff for one internal tenant. Observed ~4% mapping false positives due to email aliasing. Action: add canonical id mapping and normalize attributes.

2025-01-28: Design review with PM and Security. Security requested per-region KMS usage and explicit consent UI for customers. PM requested per-tenant scheduling cadence and reviewer assignment fields in Console.

2025-01-31: Eng review: prototype worker uses existing eventstream consumer; flagged that SCIM provider rate limits will require exponential backoff and batching. Added a backoff strategy to technical plan.
2025-02-03: GitHub PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/10682 (proof-of-concept for bundle manifest and KMS signing). Awaiting code review from @marcus and @danielle.

2025-02-05: Blocker found: identity provider for AcmeCorp lacks SCIM delta endpoint; mitigation: implement full-list reconciliation with cursor checkpointing and incremental caching. Created follow-up ENG-97765 to track provider-specific adapters.
2025-02-06: Security review scheduled 2025-02-10. Added integration test plan to ensure signed bundles verify with platform public key and optional customer public keys.
Next steps: finish SCIM adapter for Okta, implement per-tenant retention metadata in manifest, wire Console review queue, and begin pilot onboarding with Customer Success.
